stories.headline: Russian drone strikes Ukraine's SBU headquarters in Kyiv as US envoys prepare peace mission
stories.body:
A Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine's SBU security services in Kyiv on Friday. The attack injured at least 12 people, according to Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of directly targeting the personal office of the SBU chief during the daytime strike. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga described the strike on the SBU central building on Volodymyrska Street as a major escalation.

The acting head of the SBU, Oleksandr Poklad, was not inside the building during the attack and was unharmed. This was the first time the SBU headquarters had been hit since Russia began its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Russia currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory.

The strike occurred as United States envoys prepared to travel to the region. US President Donald Trump announced on Friday that special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are traveling to Kyiv and Moscow to present a proposal aimed at ending the war. Russian state news agency TASS reported that Witkoff and Kushner will visit Moscow on Saturday and Sunday. Zelenskyy said that the envoys will visit Ukraine on Sunday. This trip marks their first journey to Ukraine since Trump returned to power.

Zelenskyy proposed a temporary ceasefire during the visits of Witkoff and Kushner. He said that Ukraine would conduct no airstrikes if Russia agrees to a ceasefire during the peace talks. Zelenskyy also confirmed that Ukraine agreed to keep Russian airspace operating normally so the US envoys can travel safely.

On Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke at an international economic forum. Putin said that there are chances for a peace deal. But he maintained his demands for territorial concessions from Ukraine. Trump attributed the war to a personality problem between Zelenskyy and Putin. Trump said that both leaders truly hate each other.

A July study by the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimates the war has cost Russia around 450,000 lives. The same study estimates that Ukraine has suffered between 125,000 and 150,000 fatalities. Russian strikes continued in other parts of Ukraine overnight. An assault on the Odesa region killed one person and injured five others, including a child. Overnight strikes in the Dnipro region killed two police officials.

stories.headline: UN General Assembly votes to adopt new world map accurately representing Africa's size
stories.body:
The UN General Assembly voted 164 to 1 to adopt a resolution replacing traditional world maps with a new map. The resolution, named Correct the Map, adopts a map projection that accurately represents the size of Africa. Six countries abstained from the vote. The United States was the only country to vote against the resolution. US representative Yaryna Ferencevych criticized the resolution. Ferencevych said that debating 16th-century map projects instead of international peace mocked the General Assembly's purpose.

The traditional Mercator map shows Africa as similar in size to Greenland. In reality, Africa is 14 times larger than Greenland. African Union member states and the Bahamas sponsored the resolution. The resolution is non-legally binding and does not challenge using the Mercator map for sea and air navigation.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced that his ministry will stop using the Mercator map. Barrot said at Sorbonne University that the Mercator map gives the US, Russia, and China disproportionate visual prominence over Africa, Latin America, or Southeast Asia. France plans to switch to the Eckert IV map projection. Togolese Foreign Minister Robert Dussey said that Togo hopes to transition school geography materials away from the Mercator map by the end of the year.

stories.headline: Reform UK aides resign amid investigations into alleged election law and donation breaches
stories.body:
Two senior advisers to Reform UK leader Nigel Farage stepped down after an undercover investigation into political polling. Advisers James Orr and Dan Jukes resigned after an investigation alleged Reform UK arranged foreign-funded polling. The investigation by group Verbatim was broadcast on Channel 4. It alleged Reform UK arranged for a US company to pay over £30,000 for three opinion polls.

James Orr served as Reform UK's head of policy since February and works as an associate professor of divinity at the University of Cambridge. US Vice President JD Vance previously referred to Orr as his intellectual mentor. In undercover footage, Orr was recorded saying Farage does not know and will not know about the poll funding arrangement. Orr said the polling was paid for by an independent person and denied it benefited the party. Cambridge announced it is looking into Orr's conduct.

Undercover footage also showed Farage meeting fake US donors over lunch in Clacton. Farage described the investigation as entrapment and called the claims loose pub talk. Farage was also heckled by protesters at the party's conference in Birmingham on Friday. The Labour Party asked the Metropolitan Police to investigate potential criminal funding offences.

stories.headline: Escalating clashes between Houthis and Yemeni government forces leave dozens dead in western Yemen
stories.body:
Houthi forces launched a ground offensive on Thursday against coalition forces supporting Yemen's government-in-exile. The offensive targeted Saudi Arabia-led coalition forces in western Yemen. An AFP tally reported that 129 people have died in the renewed fighting as of Friday. A Houthi source said that more than 100 fighters from both sides have died since the attack began.

Heavy shelling and artillery fire forced hundreds of families to flee from the coastal cities of Hodeidah and Mokha. The Houthis are seeking control of ports and high ground near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The strait connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.

Yemeni government forces recaptured the al-Khazan and al-Makahna hills west of Taiz city. State television reported that a ballistic missile attack on a restaurant in al-Makha killed several civilians and injured others. The Houthis previously controlled al-Makha before government forces and the Saudi-led coalition drove them out in 2017.

stories.headline: US diesel prices hit record high amid energy market disruptions from Iran conflict
stories.body:
Average US diesel prices reached a record high of $5.85 per gallon on Friday. According to AAA, this price surpassed the previous record of $5.81 set in June 2022. US diesel prices have increased by about 55% since the US-Israeli conflict with Iran began on February 28. On that date, the national average was $3.76 a gallon. The average price of regular gasoline reached $4.15 per gallon, up from $2.98 before the war.

Brent crude oil was trading above $95 a barrel on Friday, compared to around $70 before the conflict. Distillate inventories on the US East Coast fell to a record low of 19.3 million barrels in late August. About 90% of US school buses run on diesel fuel. Russia also restricted diesel exports through September 30 after Ukrainian drones attacked Russian oil refineries.

US President Donald Trump announced an oil agreement with Venezuela to lower fuel prices. Venezuelan Interim President Delcy Rodríguez said the deal involves developing 17 oil fields. A poll showed Trump's approval rating dropped to 33%, with 31% approving of the Iran war.

stories.headline: Rescue operations continue in Nepal floods as Indian nationals remain missing and workers saved from tunnel
stories.body:
Rescuers pulled two workers alive from a flooded hydropower tunnel in Nepal after massive flash floods. Preliminary investigations show a collapsed glacier and its bedrock triggered a flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border. Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said the floods were caused by an ice-rock avalanche.

Nepalese authorities reported at least 1,295 people were killed in the disasters. More than 12,000 people have been rescued across Nepal, while almost 5,000 people remain missing. Local authorities reported that floods damaged 35 motorable bridges, 45 suspension bridges, and 40 kilometers of black-topped roads in central Nepal. A massive landslide occurred at Bhattar in Api Himal Rural Municipality. The landslide partially blocked the Chaulani River in Darchula district. The Chaulani River flows into the Mahakali River along the Nepal-India border.

The flash floods severely impacted Nepal's power sector. Almost 100% of Nepal's electricity comes from hydropower. The floods severely damaged 12 hydropower plants in the Trishuli River basin. The destruction knocked out more than 10% of Nepal's total power generation capacity. The state-owned Nepal Electricity Authority owns six of the 12 damaged facilities. The Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project was valued at about $647 million before being nearly destroyed. Overall, Nepal has 225 hydropower plants with over 3,900 megawatts of installed capacity. The country earns nearly $200 million each year exporting hydroelectricity to India and Bangladesh. In 2010, only two-thirds of Nepal's population had electricity access.

Climate factors have contributed to increasing hazards in the region. High-altitude Himalayan regions are warming 50% faster than the global average. According to disaster authorities, more than nine in 10 recorded disaster events in Nepal between 2018 and 2024 were climate-related.

The Indian government has engaged in relief and recovery efforts. India's Ministry of External Affairs reported that 275 Indian nationals remain missing after the floods. A total of 166 Indian nationals were rescued, and 1,907 Indian nationals safely crossed into Nepal from China. India supplied about 95 tonnes of relief material using seven aircraft. India also deployed 54 personnel to Nepal, including 30 tunnel rescue experts, 19 forensic experts, and a five-member medical team. In India, the Karnataka State Disaster Management Authority designated Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital in Bengaluru as the center to collect DNA samples from relatives of missing persons.

stories.headline: Air India sacks pilot after drug test confirmation following total hydraulics failure on Phuket-Delhi flight
stories.body:
Air India dismissed a pilot who tested positive for a psychoactive substance after an inflight emergency. The pilot commanded an August 4 flight from Phuket to Delhi carrying 137 passengers and crew members. The eight-year-old Airbus A320neo aircraft suffered a near-simultaneous loss of all three hydraulic systems at 36,000 feet. The flight control system detected the loss of the green hydraulic system at 9:32 am, followed four seconds later by the loss of the blue and yellow systems.

During the altitude upset, the aircraft gained 372 feet and dropped by 292 feet. The blue hydraulic system was restored shortly after 9:32 am, followed by the yellow and green systems. The aircraft landed safely at Delhi airport at 11:00 am IST. At least 24 people received medical assistance, with at least four suffering serious injuries.

Both pilots passed alcohol breath analyzer tests in Delhi. But a confirmatory blood test returned a non-negative result for a psychoactive substance for the pilot-in-command. The co-pilot tested negative. The pilot-in-command was monitoring controls rather than flying during the incident. Under civil aviation rules, pilots testing positive must undergo rehabilitation before flying again. Air India said safety is its highest priority.

The Airbus A320neo was carrying 137 passengers during the August 4 Phuket-Delhi flight.

The aircraft landed safely at Delhi airport at 11:00 am IST and taxied under its own power to the parking bay.

stories.headline: Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj detained over alleged assault on protester's father at Jantar Mantar
stories.body:
Police in Uttar Pradesh took Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj into custody after an assault investigation. Bhardwaj was detained in Bulandshahr. The detention came after a July 23 attack at Jantar Mantar during youth protests against exam irregularities. Dalit activist Nishu Aazad's father, Sanjay Kumar, was injured in the attack.

In a podcast, Bhardwaj claimed he cracked Kumar's skull and said the injury required 60 stitches. Bhardwaj claimed that he acted in self-defence after 10 to 15 people surrounded him. In a viral video, Bhardwaj claimed a phone call from Delhi minister Kapil Mishra helped him avoid arrest. Bhardwaj also made anti-Muslim statements during a podcast on September 1. He said he wants to form a hardline Hindu party to create a Muslim-free India.

The Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) filed a police complaint against Bhardwaj for falsely claiming an association with Union minister Chirag Paswan. Paswan said he takes full responsibility for pursuing the matter with Delhi Police to ensure justice. Cockroach Janta Party members protested outside Parliament Street police station demanding attempt-to-murder charges. Bhardwaj was also booked under the POCSO Act on September 4 after allegedly threatening a minor activist.
